### List arrays omit source elements **High Severity** `sourceElements` is only attached when converting a `BinaryStreamReader.ArrayValue`, but JDBC maps `Array` to `List` (`defaultTypeHintMapping`), so `ResultSet.getArray()` goes through `convert`’s `List` branch and builds `Array` without the wire values. `Array#getResultSet().getObject(i, LocalDate/LocalTime/LocalDateTime.class)` still fails with the original conversion error, so the reported issue is not fixed on the real read path. The new unit test only exercises the `ArrayValue` branch.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit f46174e5e8d69936795ec580dd43460f6a9f7abf. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Slice copies before bounds checks **Medium Severity** `getResultSet(index, count)` copies `sourceElements` before `getArray(index, count)` validates the range. With `sourceElements` set, a negative `count` throws `NegativeArraySizeException` and an out-of-range `index`/`count` throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of the `SQLException` that `getArray` previously returned.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit f46174e5e8d69936795ec580dd43460f6a9f7abf. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Nested array sources are dropped **Medium Severity** Nested date/time arrays lose `sourceElements`. Wire nested values are `ArrayValue` or `List`, not Java arrays, so `sourceValue.getClass().isArray()` is false and the nested `Array` is created with a null source. `arrayToObjectArray(arrayValue.getArray())` also does not recurse (`ArrayValue.toObjectArray()` would). Inner `getResultSet().getObject(i, LocalDate.class)` still fails for `Array(Array(Date32))` and similar types.
Additional Locations (1) - [`jdbc-v2/src/main/java/com/clickhouse/jdbc/internal/JdbcUtils.java#L354-L356`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-java/blob/f46174e5e8d69936795ec580dd43460f6a9f7abf/jdbc-v2/src/main/java/com/clickhouse/jdbc/internal/JdbcUtils.java#L354-L356)

please see comment in the issue https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-java/issues/3284#issuecomment-6940778778

Thanks @chernser, reworked following your comment on the issue (the `Array` was built from `java.sql.Date` objects): the `ValueConverters` Date/Time/Timestamp -> java.time conversions are removed. The `Array` now also keeps the elements as read from the server (e.g. `LocalDate` for Date32, `ZonedDateTime` for DateTime64), and the result set from `getResultSet()` serves `getObject(i, LocalDate/LocalTime/LocalDateTime.class)` from those values, so nothing is round-tripped through `java.sql.Date/Time/Timestamp` and the JVM time zone is not involved. `getArray()` and default `getObject(i)` still return the java.sql types. The new test runs with a default zone whose DST gap would shift a Timestamp round trip (00:30 -> 01:30) and passes; `ArrayResultSetTest` 41/41. Not covered: Time64 sub-millisecond precision when read as `java.sql.Time`.
